title: Spec-first or issue-first
body: Start from local proposal.md/tasks.md or pull an existing issue tracker issue with specsync pull.

title: Works in repos with no openspec/
body: specsync init (or pull -init) makes a scratch openspec/ that git never sees, so an agent can pull an issue and sync in any repo. Nothing is created unless you ask; a user-level default store is also supported.

title: Design notes survive the worktree
body: A design.md renders as ## Design notes in the synced issue, so decisions made while planning aren't lost if the local worktree is force-removed. Oversized notes overflow to a linked issue comment instead of getting truncated.

title: Planning scan
body: specsync scan shows what already exists for an area — in-flight changes, loose issues, recent commits — before you plan.

title: See who's already working what
body: specsync status shows where your work stands: pull request, checks, review, unpushed and uncommitted work, how far the base has moved and whether a merge would conflict — with the commands to catch up. Under an epic or with blockers it also lists every related item across your repos, and how to pick each piece up again, including its agent session through an optional provider. Read-only, and -json gives agents the same facts.

title: All your work, across repos
body: specsync overview lists every change, worktree and open request in the clones under your workspace, grouped by epic, then work under no epic, then branches with no change. Scope it with -repo, -epic, -mine, -attention, -stage or -unattached. Read-only; -json for agents.

title: Spin off emergent work
body: specsync spinoff spawns a new linked change from a discovery, keeping the parent scoped and marking the source task as moved.

title: Capture ideas
body: specsync idea "Thought" files a vague or elaborate idea as a GitHub issue in your ideas inbox; specsync ideas lists open intake. Graduate with specsync pull -issue <n>.

title: Idempotent
body: Run specsync -change my-change as often as needed. If the issue tracker issue already exists, specsync updates it (same identity marker) instead of creating a duplicate.

title: Adopt an existing issue
body: specsync adopt -issue 3691 -change my-change binds a change and an issue that already exist independently, writing the ref cache before touching the issue body so the link holds immediately instead of racing search indexing.

title: Workflow state management
body: Set stage explicitly with specsync set-stage my-change [active|blocked|in-review|complete] so progress is visible and committed in metadata.

title: The branch names the change
body: Inside a change's worktree, set-stage, note and archive find the change from the branch — feat/42-my-change or an Orca workspace's user/my-change. On main nothing resolves, so an agent there can't act on a change by accident.

title: Start work as an Orca workspace
body: With worktrees.launcher: orca, specsync start my-change creates the change's worktree through Orca, linked to its issue, so Orca's agent gets the spec as its brief. It checks Orca kept the branch and leaves it unpublished until you push.

title: Orca workspaces stay in step
body: Run specsync workspace setup and workspace archive from orca.yaml hooks: a workspace started from an issue becomes a change, its stage goes active, and it goes back to derived when the workspace is archived.

title: Priority-driven dispatch
body: Set priorities (1-100) with specsync set-priority my-change 85. Agents respect priority when deciding what to work on next — humans direct focus.

title: Projects board sync
body: Project and sync with specsync -change my-change -project my-org/6. Add -status-map "active=In Progress,complete=Done" to align board columns with change stages.

title: Release follow-up
body: specsync release-plan highlights shipped changes, loose/unlinked work, archive candidates, and advisory release impact from spec-level deltas.

title: Spec-driven changelog
body: specsync changelog writes a Keep a Changelog section from your shipped changes — one entry per change, release notes authored at planning time, never a raw commit dump.

title: Archive audit
body: specsync audit cross-references archived changes against GitHub PRs to find archived-but-unmerged work. Add -mark-shipped to record the final lifecycle step.

title: Spec ↔ issue linker
body: specsync resolves a change's issue from branch name (feat/42-my-change), issue marker, or ref cache — so pull without -issue and idempotent sync update the right issue instead of creating duplicates.

title: Cross-repo epic scaffolding
body: specsync epic "Feature X" --repo org/planning --child org/backend#12 --child frontend-slug mints a coordination issue and wires every child — local change or existing issue, any repo — to it, idempotently.

title: CLI self-documentation
body: specsync agent-help provides command guidance without manuals. Use --json for machine-readable schema suitable for agents and automation.

title: Agent skill diagnostics
body: specsync doctor detects and diagnoses AI agent skill installations (Claude Code, OpenCode, Copilot, etc.), analyzes token usage, checks that the openspec CLI dependency is installed and reachable, and recommends fixes.

title: Any MCP-connected tracker
body: -provider mcp projects changes through any external MCP server instead of gh — Linear, Jira, GitHub, or in-house. Speaks the current MCP spec with automatic fallback to legacy handshake-based servers.

title: A clean issue, not a wall of text
body: A synced issue shows title and task checklist first — Proposal, Original ask, and Discoveries render inside collapsed <details> blocks, one click away, nothing removed.

title: Catch stale references in your docs
body: specsync verify -refs finds commit hashes and issue or PR references in change documents that no longer resolve after a rebase. Read-only and advisory; it never guesses a replacement.

title: Warns before a pull request is too big
body: specsync status and verify -size flag a branch that is over a files, lines or commits budget, or that mixes commit scopes, before review starts. Advisory by default; -fail-on-oversized makes it a gate.

title: Define your flow once, get the next step
body: Declare gates and steps in openspec/specsync.yml; specsync next reads the work's state and prints the next step and its command, specsync flow marks where you are. Commands from the repo run only after specsync trust.

title: A map for reviewing a big pull request
body: specsync review-map turns a branch into a checklist: the paths the author declared as needing judgement first, then each commit with its files and sizes, then totals by category. -equivalent proves a rewritten branch holds the same content.

title: Short, consistent issues and PRs
body: specsync lint checks titles, headers, sentences and length against a short standard, advisory unless -fail. pr-body -template writes a brief PR body from the change and your repo's template. Never rewrites your text.

title: Plan a big change as slices
body: Declare reviewable slices in tasks.md, each with a contract, an order and a size budget. specsync slices shows each slice's branch and pull request, slice start opens the next one stacked on the last, and sync -slices mirrors them as child issues.

title: Clean up finished work safely
body: specsync cleanup lists worktrees whose work is provably merged and, with -apply, removes them and their branches. It never touches dirty trees, ignored files, protected or shared branches, unpushed commits, open requests or live sessions, and re-checks each one just before removal; hooks run only after specsync trust.

title: The same steps every time
body: new, start, save, gates, update and pr prep/open do the mechanical parts of starting, checking and opening work, each with a dry run. They refuse secrets, forbidden trailers, unsafe pushes and unconfirmed PRs; the conventions come from openspec/specsync.yml.
